## Rules (MANDATORY)
- **Issue-first**: Create a devdash issue BEFORE writing code. No exceptions.
- **Issue-per-commit**: Every git commit must map to a devdash issue. If scope expands, create new issues.
- **Mark in-progress**: `devdash update <id> --status=in_progress` before starting work.
- **Pre-commit checkpoint**: Before each `git commit`, verify you have an issue. If not, create one.
- **Close after push**: Only close issues after `git push` succeeds — never before.
- **No orphaned work**: At session end, every commit must map to a closed issue.
- **Path**: `/Users/jason/.local/bin/devdash`
- **Preserve stderr**: Avoid `2>/dev/null` on devdash commands — stderr contains error details you'll need for debugging failures.
- **Prohibited**: Do NOT use `bd`, TodoWrite, TaskCreate, or markdown files for task tracking

## Quick Reference
- **Start (task already named)**: `devdash show <id>` → `devdash update <id> --status=in_progress`
- **Start (need a task)**: `devdash ready` → `devdash show <id>` → `devdash update <id> --status=in_progress`
- **Complete**: git add → commit → push → `devdash close <id> --summary="..." --commit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)`
- **Report**: `devdash report <id> --status=code_complete|committed|pushed|error --summary="..."`
- Close summaries are institutional memory — include what, why, decisions, surprises, follow-ups.
- One issue per commit. Scope creep = new issue. Multi-step = parent + children.

## Output Formats
- There is no `--json` flag. Do not try `--json`, `--format`, or `--output`.
- These commands already return JSON: `show`, `find`, `activity`, `comments`, `jobs show`, `score <id>`, `token list`, `sync`
- All other commands return human-readable text. Parse UUIDs from `create`/`close`/`update` output directly.

## On-Demand Reference
Run these when you need detailed guidance:
- `devdash help cli` — Full command reference (flags, ID formats, --since syntax)
- `devdash help workflow` — When to create issues, decomposition patterns, bead relationships
- `devdash help close` — Close summary expectations with examples
- `devdash help pr` — PR footer format and multi-issue PRs
- `devdash help projects` — Cross-project dependencies and multi-repo work
- `devdash help report` — Progress reporting cadence and status values

Explore the notifications system in the dev-dash repo at /Users/jason/playground/claudespace/dev-dash. I want a comprehensive picture of:

1. **Backend / served data**:
   - Where notifications are defined (DB schema, tables, columns)
   - API routes/endpoints that serve them (list, mark-read, etc.)
   - How/when notifications are *created* — what events trigger a notification (issue assigned, PR comment, agent finished, etc.)
   - Whether there's a real-time channel (SSE, websockets) pushing them
   - Any background jobs that generate or clean them up

2. **Relevance / filtering**:
   - How notifications are scoped to a user (user_id, project membership, etc.)
   - Read vs unread state, dismissed state
   - Any preferences/settings that gate which notifications a user sees

3. **Frontend / UI**:
   - Which React components render notifications (bell icon, dropdown, full page, toast?)
   - Where in the layout they appear
   - How they're fetched (polling, SSE subscription, hook name)
   - What actions a user can take (mark read, click-through, dismiss)

Look in server/src/ for routes/db schema and client/src/ for components/hooks. The repo uses Express + SQLite (Drizzle migration in progress) on the backend and Vite + React on the frontend.

Report findings as a structured summary with file paths and line numbers (file_path:line_number format) for the key pieces. Aim for thorough but readable — under 600 words. Call out any gaps, dead code, or things that look broken.

content.text:
Perfect. Now I have a comprehensive picture. Let me create my report.

---

## Notifications System Summary

### 1. BACKEND / SERVED DATA

**Database Schema** (server/src/db/schema.ts:231-245)
- Table: `notifications` (PostgreSQL with Drizzle)
- Columns: `id` (pk), `userId` (fk), `type`, `title`, `message`, `read` (bool, default false), `metadata` (JSON), `orgId`, `projectId`, `mentionType`, `createdAt`
- Index: `idx_notifications_user(userId, read)` for fast filtering by user + read status

**API Routes** (server/src/routes/notifications.ts)
- `GET /api/notifications` — fetch all for user, ordered newest first
- `GET /api/notifications/unread-count` — count unread (used for badge)
- `PATCH /api/notifications/:id/read` — mark single as read
- `PATCH /api/notifications/read-all` — mark all user's notifications as read
- `POST /api/notifications` — create (for testing/internal use)
- `DELETE /api/notifications/:id` — remove notification

**Notification Creation Triggers**:
- **Agent completion/failure** (server/src/services/agent-dispatch.ts:1912-1969): Type `agent_complete` or `agent_failed`; targets dispatcher, bead assignee, project owner (deduplicated)
- **Task assignment** (server/src/routes/beads.ts:733-741, 1108-1116): Type `task_assigned` when bead assigned or handed off; notifies assignee
- **@mentions in comments** (server/src/routes/bead-comments.ts:125-149): Type `mention`; extracts `@username` patterns via regex `/@([a-zA-Z0-9_-]{2,30})\b/g`, resolves to project-access users
- **Job queue failure** (server/src/services/job-queue.ts:403-410): Type `agent_failed` to project owner

**Notification Metadata**: Varies by type — includes `beadId`, `projectId`, `prUrl`, `commitSha`, `branchName`, `rescueBranch`, `commentId`, `handoff: true` flags, etc. Stored as JSON string.

**Real-Time Channel**:
- **SSE stream** (server/src/routes/events.ts): `GET /api/events?projectId=X` or `?orgId=X` broadcasts project/org events
- Event type: `notifications:new` emitted when new notification created (server/src/routes/beads.ts:742, 1117)
- Heartbeat every 30s; per-project/org/user scoped filtering
- **NOT a full notification push**: Only fires on-change event, client must poll `/notifications` endpoint

**Cleanup**:
- `notificationOps.deleteOld(userId, interval)` exists (server/src/db/ops.ts:852) but is **UNUSED in production** — only tested

### 2. RELEVANCE / FILTERING

**User Scoping**:
- `userId` foreign key ensures user isolation; no org/project level notifications to all members
- Task assignments & agent events sent to **specific users** (dispatcher, assignee, owner)
- Mentions only to resolved project members with access (server/src/services/mention-parser.ts:21-33)

**Read/Unread State**:
- Boolean `read` column (default false)
- No "dismissed" or "archived" state — only `read` or deleted
- `markRead()` and `markAllRead()` cover individual and bulk mark-read

**Preferences/Settings**: **NONE implemented**
- No notification type filters or opt-out mechanism in schema
- Frontend lets users filter locally (client-side only), but server delivers all types

### 3. FRONTEND / UI

**Components**:
- **NotificationBell** (client/src/components/notifications/NotificationBell.tsx): Bell icon in navbar with dropdown, badge shows unread count (99+ cap), displays latest 5 notifications, "View all notifications" link
- **Notifications page** (client/src/pages/Notifications.tsx): Full-page list with type/unread filters, delete button per notification

**Data Fetching**:
- `useNotifications()` hook: Polling via React Query, **refetchInterval: 30s** (client/src/hooks/useNotifications.ts:15)
- `useUnreadCount()` hook: Polling every **15s** (line 29) — more frequent badge updates
- No SSE subscription on client (events.ts only used for beads/jobs, not notifications)
- No WebSocket

**User Actions**:
- Mark as read (single or all)
- Delete (remove from view)
- Click-through (metadata.link unused; no navigation implemented)

**Icons/Visual**: Green checkmark for `agent_complete`, red alert for `agent_failed`, purple CPU for task events, info icon default

---

## GAPS & ISSUES

1. **'mention' notification type UNDEFINED** (server/src/routes/bead-comments.ts:140 uses it, but packages/api-types/src/schemas/enums.ts:49-51 excludes it) — type mismatch; Zod validation may reject at API boundary
2. **No notification cleanup**: `deleteOld()` never called; old notifications accumulate indefinitely
3. **No user preferences**: All notification types forced; no per-user opt-outs or quiet hours
4. **Polling lag**: 30s refetch means up to 30s delay in seeing agent completions; SSE not wired for real-time
5. **Unused POST /notifications endpoint**: Marked "for internal/testing" but open to any authenticated user
6. **No notification categories**: All live in one notification center; no separation (e.g., mentions vs system)
7. **Metadata.link never used**: Frontend doesn't navigate to referenced beads/projects on click

---

## KEY FILES

| File | Lines | Purpose |
|------|-------|---------|
| server/src/db/schema.ts | 231–245 | Notifications table definition |
| server/src/db/ops.ts | 823–854 | CRUD operations (notificationOps) |
| server/src/routes/notifications.ts | 1–134 | API endpoint handlers |
| server/src/services/agent-dispatch.ts | 1912–1969 | Notification creation on job completion |
| server/src/routes/beads.ts | 733–741, 1108–1116 | Task assignment notifications |
| server/src/routes/bead-comments.ts | 125–149 | Mention detection & notification creation |
| server/src/services/mention-parser.ts | 8–15 | @mention regex & resolution |
| server/src/routes/events.ts | 44–79 | SSE channel (broadcasts `notifications:new` event) |
| client/src/hooks/useNotifications.ts | 1–82 | React Query hooks (polling 30s/15s) |
| client/src/components/notifications/NotificationBell.tsx | 1–219 | Navbar bell icon + dropdown UI |
| client/src/pages/Notifications.tsx | 1–284 | Full notifications page with filters |
| packages/api-types/src/schemas/enums.ts | 49–51 | NotificationType enum (missing 'mention') |

content.text:
# Prioritized Fix Plan

The lens here: this is a shared backend with N client UIs (`dd-red`, `dd-green`, `dd-yellow`, `devdash-pink/blue`, `devdash-cli-go`, etc.). That changes the calculus — **API contract and delivery are server-side concerns that benefit every client; UX polish is per-client**. So the server work must land first and be stable before clients can build against it.

Adding the configuration angle reframes things too: clients shouldn't each invent their own "mute settings" — preferences belong on the server so a user's choices follow them between UIs.

## Phase 1 — Contract correctness (blocks everything downstream)

These are cheap, but every other fix assumes them.

1. **Fix `mention` type enum mismatch** — `bead-comments.ts:140` writes `'mention'` but `packages/api-types/.../enums.ts:49` doesn't list it. Any client doing Zod validation drops these rows silently. *Backend + shared types.*
2. **Lock down `POST /api/notifications`** — currently any authed user can self-inject. Restrict to internal/service or require admin scope.
3. **Define & document the notification payload contract** — write down what `metadata` is allowed to carry per `type` (e.g., `agent_complete` always has `{ jobId, beadId, prUrl?, commitSha? }`). Without this, every client invents its own click-through logic. This becomes the source of truth shared types reference.

## Phase 2 — Real-time delivery (foundation for every client)

4. **Wire SSE delivery for notifications** — server already broadcasts `notifications:new` on `/api/events` but the payload is event-only. Make it carry the full notification row, scoped per-user (not per-project, since notifications are user-targeted). Then clients subscribe instead of polling. Per your stated preference, this is the right fix — not bumping the poll interval down. Each client UI then gets a thin `useNotificationsStream()` hook.

## Phase 3 — Configuration model (the new capability you raised)

This needs design alignment before code. Proposing:

5. **Schema: `notification_preferences`** — scoped rules with resolution order *user override > project default > system default*:
   - `scope`: `user` | `project` | `org`
   - `scopeId`: fk
   - `type`: notification type (or `*` for all)
   - `action`: `deliver` | `mute` | `digest`
   - `channels`: array of `in_app` | `email` | `webhook` (future)
   - `quietHoursStart/End` (user scope only)

6. **API: preferences CRUD** — `GET/PUT /api/notifications/preferences` (mine), `GET/PUT /api/projects/:id/notification-defaults` (project admins). Returns merged effective preferences so clients don't replicate resolution logic.

7. **Plumb preferences into creation paths** — `notificationOps.create()` checks effective prefs and skips/digests/routes accordingly. Single chokepoint so every trigger (`agent-dispatch`, `beads`, `bead-comments`, `job-queue`) gets it for free.

> **Open question for you**: do we want **delivery channels** (email, webhook) in the v1 schema even if only `in_app` is implemented, so we don't migrate again? My vote: yes, schema supports it, only `in_app` is wired.

> **Open question**: **digest mode** — worth it now, or v2? It implies a scheduled job, batching logic, and a "digest delivered" state. I'd defer.

## Phase 4 — Lifecycle / hygiene

8. **Cleanup job for old notifications** — `notificationOps.deleteOld()` exists but is never called. Wire it into the existing job scheduler. Decide retention (30d? 90d? configurable per-org?).
9. **Decide read vs dismissed vs archived** — currently only `read` + delete. If we add `dismissed`, the bell can hide dismissed-but-unread items without losing them. Small schema change, big UX flexibility for clients.

## Phase 5 — Per-client UX (each UI does its own)

10. **Click-through targets** — once Phase 1.3 contract is set, clients can each render meaningful navigation. Not a server task but **dev-dash main UI** should be the reference implementation.
11. **Categories / grouping** — server returns notifications with a `category` derived from type (`mentions`, `agents`, `assignments`, `system`); clients decide how to display.

---

## What I'd skip (or defer)

- **WebSockets** — SSE is already in the codebase and sufficient. Don't introduce a second channel.
- **Digest/batching v1** — defer until prefs land and we see if anyone asks.
- **Email/Slack delivery v1** — schema-ready, not implemented.

---

## Proposed dd issues (for your review before creation)

I'd structure as a **parent epic** (`Notifications system overhaul`) with these children, in dependency order:

| # | Title | Phase | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fix `mention` notification type missing from shared enum | 1 | One-line fix + regenerate types |
| 2 | Restrict `POST /api/notifications` to internal callers | 1 | Auth middleware change |
| 3 | Document notification payload contract per type | 1 | Markdown in `server/docs/` + tighten metadata typing |
| 4 | Deliver notifications over SSE (replace client polling) | 2 | Server payload + client hook + remove `refetchInterval` |
| 5 | Design notification preferences schema (user/project/org) | 3 | Design issue — produces a doc, not code |
| 6 | Implement notification_preferences table + migration | 3 | Depends on #5 |
| 7 | Preferences API (mine + project defaults) | 3 | Depends on #6 |
| 8 | Apply preferences in `notificationOps.create()` chokepoint | 3 | Depends on #7 |
| 9 | Wire `notificationOps.deleteOld()` into scheduled job | 4 | Independent of preferences |
| 10 | Add `dismissed` state (schema + API) | 4 | Independent; small |
| 11 | Reference click-through implementation in dev-dash main UI | 5 | Per-client; depends on #3 |

**Before I create these**, three things to confirm:

1. **Scope**: should I open issues against `dev-dash` (`896b3dbc`) only, or also stub corresponding tracking issues in the variant projects (`dd-red`, `dd-green`, `dd-yellow`, `devdash-pink`, etc.) for the per-client work?
2. **Channels in v1 schema**: yes/no on including email/webhook columns now even though only `in_app` works?
3. **Project-level overrides**: are project admins a concept that exists today, or do I need to gate #7 on building admin roles first? (I can check, but easier to ask.)

Once you answer those I'll create the parent + children with proper `--parent` linkage and dependency edges.

The server's job for notifications is narrow:

- Deliver them (REST + SSE) with a clean, documented payload contract
- Track universal user state (read/unread, possibly dismissed)

Don't propose server-side preferences tables, preferences APIs, or per-project notification defaults stored on the backend.

Saved. Here's the revised plan with the preferences chunk removed:

# Revised Plan — Server stays narrow

The server's job for notifications collapses to three things:
1. **Create** notifications on triggering events
2. **Deliver** them with a clean, documented contract (REST + SSE)
3. **Track universal user state** (read/unread)

Everything else — mute lists, type filters, channel routing, team rules, quiet hours — lives in each variant client. dev-dash blue configures its own. dd-red configures its own. They don't talk to each other.

## Phase 1 — Contract correctness

1. **Fix `mention` type missing from shared enum** — `bead-comments.ts` writes it; `packages/api-types/.../enums.ts` doesn't list it. Silent validation drops in any client doing Zod parsing.
2. **Lock down `POST /api/notifications`** — currently any authed user can self-inject. Restrict to internal service callers.
3. **Document the notification payload contract per type** — what `metadata` is allowed to carry for each `type` (e.g., `agent_complete` → `{ jobId, beadId, prUrl?, commitSha? }`). This is the source of truth every variant client builds against. Tighten the shared types once written down.

## Phase 2 — Real-time delivery

4. **Wire SSE delivery for notifications** — server already emits `notifications:new` on `/api/events` but only as a poke; carry the full notification payload, scoped per-user. Variant clients subscribe; no more polling. (Per your standing preference — fix the SSE, don't tune the poll.)

## Phase 3 — Lifecycle / hygiene

5. **Wire `notificationOps.deleteOld()` into the scheduled job runner** — exists, never called, table grows unbounded. Pick a default retention (90d?); revisit later if anyone complains.
6. **(Optional) add `dismissed` state** — purely a question of whether "dismissed but not deleted" is useful universal state. If yes, server-side. If clients can live with read+delete, skip it. **Want your call here.**

## Phase 4 — Per-client work (one issue per variant later)

7. **Reference click-through implementation in dev-dash blue** — once Phase 1.3 is locked, blue becomes the reference for navigating from a notification to its target (bead, PR, job). Other variants can mirror or diverge as their UX warrants.

## What's gone vs. last plan

- ❌ `notification_preferences` schema
- ❌ Preferences API
- ❌ Plumbing prefs into the create chokepoint
- ❌ Email/webhook channel columns
- ❌ Project-admin defaults
- ❌ Digest mode

That's ~5 issues that evaporate. The server work shrinks from "build a preferences system" to "ship a clean contract and a real-time pipe."

## Proposed dd issues (review before I create)

Parent epic: **Notifications system overhaul** (against `dev-dash` / `896b3dbc`)

| # | Title | Phase | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fix `mention` notification type missing from shared enum | 1 | — |
| 2 | Restrict `POST /api/notifications` to internal callers | 1 | — |
| 3 | Document notification payload contract per type (+ tighten metadata typing) | 1 | — |
| 4 | Deliver notifications over SSE; remove client polling | 2 | #3 |
| 5 | Wire `notificationOps.deleteOld()` into scheduled job runner | 3 | — |
| 6 | (optional) Add `dismissed` state to notifications | 3 | — |
| 7 | Reference click-through implementation in dev-dash blue UI | 4 | #3 |

**Two things to confirm before I create them:**

1. **#6 — `dismissed` state, yes or no?** It's universal user state so it would be server-side, but only worth doing if you want it. If clients are fine with read+delete, I'll drop it.
2. **Project for #7** — when you say "dev-dash blue is the base env," do you mean issue #7 should be filed against `devdash-blue` (`f7730420`), or against `dev-dash` (`896b3dbc`) main? I had been assuming the main client lives in `client/` of the dev-dash repo and the variants are separate repos — confirm where the "blue" reference UI actually lives so #7 lands in the right project.

Once you answer those I'll create the parent + children with `--parent` linkage.

This issue produces the source of truth that #4 (SSE delivery) and #7 (click-through) build against.

## Deliverable
A markdown doc (server/docs/notifications-contract.md or similar) listing every NotificationType and the exact metadata shape it guarantees. Example:

  - agent_complete: { jobId, beadId, projectId, prUrl?, commitSha?, branchName? }
  - agent_failed:   { jobId, beadId, projectId, rescueBranch?, errorSummary? }
  - task_assigned:  { beadId, projectId, handoff?: boolean, fromUserId? }
  - mention:        { beadId, commentId, projectId, mentionedBy }

## Steps
1. Audit every notificationOps.create() call site to enumerate what each writes today
2. Pick a canonical shape per type (closest to current usage, fill gaps)
3. Tighten the metadata typing in packages/api-types — discriminated union by type
4. Update creation sites to match
5. Write the doc

## Acceptance
- Doc exists and lists every type
- Shared types enforce per-type metadata via discriminated union
- All in-tree creation sites compile against the new types
- Blocks #4 and #7"

Per project preference, polling is not the right fix; the SSE pipe should carry full notification payloads.

## Depends on
- #3 (payload contract) — SSE messages must conform to the documented contract

## Server changes
- server/src/routes/events.ts: when emitting 'notifications:new', include the full notification row, scoped per-user (not per-project — notifications are user-targeted)
- Verify scoping: a user subscribed to /api/events should only receive notifications:new events for their own userId, regardless of which projectId/orgId they passed
- Audit every notificationOps.create() call site to ensure each one publishes to the SSE bus after insert (today only some paths do)

## Client changes (dev-dash main UI only — variant clients update on their own cadence)
- client/src/hooks/useNotifications.ts: subscribe to the SSE stream, push new notifications into the React Query cache, drop refetchInterval
- Same for useUnreadCount
- Keep an initial REST fetch on mount; SSE handles updates after that
- Reconnection: on SSE reconnect, do a single REST refetch to catch anything missed during the gap

## Acceptance
- A new notification appears in the bell/dropdown within ~1s of creation, not 30s
- No periodic /api/notifications GET requests in network tab once subscribed
- SSE drop+reconnect recovers state correctly"

devdash create --parent=1701f49f-656f-473b-8d1e-f4e45683f5d7 --title="Wire notificationOps.deleteOld() into scheduled job runner" --type=task --priority=3 --description="notificationOps.deleteOld(userId, interval) exists in server/src/db/ops.ts but is never called anywhere in production. The notifications table grows unbounded.

## Fix
- Identify the existing scheduled job runner in server/src/services/ (the same one running other periodic tasks — verify before editing)
- Add a daily job that calls deleteOld() across all users with a default retention window

- Log how many rows were pruned per run

## Acceptance

- Logged metric visible in server logs
- No new config surface"

devdash create --parent=1701f49f-656f-473b-8d1e-f4e45683f5d7 --title="Add 'dismissed' state to notifications" --type=enhancement --priority=3 --description="Today the only notification state is 'read' (boolean) plus delete. Adding a 'dismissed' state lets clients hide notifications from the bell/dropdown without losing them from history, and gives variant UIs more flexibility in how they surface things.

Dismissed is universal user state (lives on the server), unlike preferences/filters which are client-side.

## Schema
- Add dismissed boolean column (default false) to notifications table
- Migration in server/src/db/migrations/ following the existing Drizzle pattern
- Update server/src/db/schema.ts and server/src/db/ops.ts

## API

## Shared types
- Add dismissed to the Notification type in packages/api-types

## Out of scope
- Auto-dismiss rules
- Client UI changes — each variant decides how to expose dismissal

## Acceptance
- Schema migration applied cleanly
- New endpoints functional with auth
- Existing GET behavior unchanged when includeDismissed not specified"

devdash create --parent=1701f49f-656f-473b-8d1e-f4e45683f5d7 --title="Reference click-through implementation in dev-dash main UI" --type=enhancement --priority=2 --description="Once #3 (payload contract) lands, the dev-dash main UI (client/src/) becomes the reference implementation for navigating from a notification to its target. Today the bell and notifications page render notifications as read-only breadcrumbs — clicking them does nothing.

Variant UIs (red, green, yellow, pink, blue) will mirror or diverge from this as their UX warrants — out of scope here.

- #3 (payload contract) — click target derivation must use the documented metadata shape

## Click target rules (per type, derived from contract)
- agent_complete / agent_failed: navigate to the bead detail view, with PR link surfaced if metadata.prUrl exists
- task_assigned: navigate to the assigned bead
- mention: navigate to the bead with the comment anchored (use metadata.commentId if hash anchors are supported, else just the bead)
- system / fallback: no navigation

## Components to update
- client/src/components/notifications/NotificationBell.tsx (dropdown items)
- client/src/pages/Notifications.tsx (full-page list rows)

- Clicking a notification marks it read AND navigates
- Cmd/Ctrl-click opens in new tab (use anchor tags, not onClick on a div)
- Mark-read should not block navigation — fire-and-forget the mutation

- Every notification type has a defined click behavior (or explicit no-op)
- Clicking from the bell dropdown navigates AND closes the dropdown
- Clicking from the notifications page navigates AND visually marks the row read"

# Notifications System Overhaul — Execution Plan

## Context

The notifications backend serves multiple variant UIs (dev-dash main, blue, red, green, yellow, pink, cli-go). Audit found seven issues ranging from a silent-drop enum mismatch to an unbuilt SSE pipe to an unbounded-growth table. User confirmed that notification **preferences** are client-side (each variant owns its own config) — so the server work collapses to: fix the contract, deliver in real-time, keep the table healthy, add universal state (dismissed), and build a reference click-through implementation in the dev-dash main UI. This plan is the execution coordinator; comprehensive detail lives in the dd issues below.

## Work graph (dd issues)

Parent epic: `1701f49f` — Notifications system overhaul

| ID | Phase | Title | Depends on | Parallelizable |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ae2bd37e` | 1 | Fix `mention` notification type missing from shared enum | — | ✅ wave 1 |
| `051efa22` | 1 | Restrict `POST /api/notifications` to internal callers | — | ✅ wave 1 |
| `d842ca69` | 3 | Wire `notificationOps.deleteOld()` into scheduled job runner | — | ✅ wave 1 |
| `2f62374d` | 3 | Add `dismissed` state to notifications | — | ✅ wave 1 |
| `98e41597` | 1 | Document notification payload contract per type (+ tighten metadata typing) | — | ❌ main thread (load-bearing) |
| `03ab1f97` | 2 | Deliver notifications over SSE; remove client polling | `98e41597` | ✅ wave 3 |
| `1c6a6372` | 4 | Reference click-through implementation in dev-dash main UI | `98e41597` | ✅ wave 3 |

Each dd issue carries acceptance criteria, file paths (flagged as memory snapshots to verify), and step-by-step notes. Read the dd before starting each issue — do not re-derive scope from this plan.

## Execution strategy

### Setup

1. Enter a git worktree for the whole overhaul (branch `notifications-overhaul`). All waves land in this worktree; final PR bundles commits, one commit per dd issue.
2. `devdash update <id> --status=in_progress` as each issue is picked up; `devdash close <id>` only after the commit is pushed (per workflow rules — git push precedes close, never parallel).

### Wave 1 — Independent quick wins (parallel subagents)

Launch up to four general-purpose subagents in a single message, one per issue. Each subagent:
- Reads its dd issue for full context: `devdash show <id>`
- Implements the change in the shared worktree
- Runs `npx tsc --noEmit` from `server/` before reporting done
- Reports back a short summary of what changed and where

Issues: `ae2bd37e`, `051efa22`, `d842ca69`, `2f62374d`.

**Conflict surface to watch**: `2f62374d` adds a `dismissed` column to `notifications` schema + ops; `ae2bd37e` touches the shared `NotificationType` enum. Different files — should not collide. If Drizzle migration ordering matters, main thread serializes the migration file creation.

After all four subagents report, main thread:
- Reviews each change
- Runs one consolidated `npx tsc --noEmit` in `server/`
- Commits each issue separately (one commit per dd)
- Pushes
- Closes each dd with an institutional-memory summary

### Wave 2 — Payload contract (main thread, sequential)

Issue: `98e41597`.

Done on main thread because it's load-bearing: it audits every `notificationOps.create()` call site, enumerates the metadata shapes in use, picks the canonical shape per type, introduces a discriminated union in `packages/api-types`, and updates creation sites to match. Wave 1 must be merged first so the audit sees final enum + dismissed state.

Deliverable includes both:
- `server/docs/notifications-contract.md` (or similar)
- Tightened types in `packages/api-types/src/schemas/`

Commit, push, close.

### Wave 3 — Unblocked downstream work (parallel subagents)

Once `98e41597` is closed, launch two general-purpose subagents in parallel:
- Subagent A: `03ab1f97` (server SSE payload + scoping + client hook rewrite in `client/src/hooks/useNotifications.ts`)
- Subagent B: `1c6a6372` (dev-dash main UI click-through — bell dropdown, notifications page, `deriveClickTarget` helper)

These touch mostly disjoint files (server/routes/events.ts + client hook vs. client components/notifications + pages/Notifications). Minimal conflict risk.

Each subagent reads its dd for full context, implements, runs `npx tsc --noEmit` in both `server/` and `client/`, reports back. Main thread reviews, commits each separately, pushes, closes.

## Critical files (verify before editing — memory snapshots may be stale)

- `server/src/db/schema.ts` — notifications table
- `server/src/db/ops.ts` — `notificationOps` (create/list/markRead/deleteOld)
- `server/src/routes/notifications.ts` — REST handlers
- `server/src/routes/events.ts` — SSE channel (broadcasts `notifications:new`)
- `server/src/routes/bead-comments.ts` — mention creation path
- `server/src/routes/beads.ts` — task_assigned creation paths (assignment + handoff)
- `server/src/services/agent-dispatch.ts` — agent_complete/agent_failed creation
- `server/src/services/job-queue.ts` — job-failure agent_failed creation
- `server/src/services/mention-parser.ts` — @mention regex + resolution
- `packages/api-types/src/schemas/enums.ts` — `NotificationType`
- `packages/api-types/src/schemas/` (wherever Notification payload type lives) — shared type
- `client/src/hooks/useNotifications.ts` — polling hook → SSE subscription
- `client/src/components/notifications/NotificationBell.tsx` — bell + dropdown
- `client/src/pages/Notifications.tsx` — full-page list

## Verification

Per phase, not per issue — issues have their own acceptance criteria.

**After wave 1**:
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean in `server/`
- Manually POST a notification as a normal authed user → expect 403/404
- Drizzle migration runs cleanly against dev DB; `notifications.dismissed` column exists
- Scheduled job runner logs show the cleanup task registered

**After wave 2**:
- Contract doc committed and reviewed
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean in `server/` and `client/` — discriminated union narrows correctly at every `notificationOps.create()` call site
- No call site uses `any` for metadata

**After wave 3**:
- Deploy to dev Railway environment
- Trigger a notification end-to-end (assign a bead, or wait for an agent job to complete)
- Network tab: no periodic `/api/notifications` GETs; SSE stream shows `notifications:new` with full payload
- Notification appears in bell within ~1s
- Click notification in bell → navigates to target (bead/PR), closes dropdown, marks read
- Click notification in notifications page → navigates and marks row read
- Cmd-click opens in new tab

**Final**:
- `devdash show 1701f49f` shows all 7 children closed
- Open one bundled PR against `main` referencing all 7 dd IDs in footer

## Notes

- **Tool call ordering**: `devdash close` runs sequentially AFTER `git push` succeeds, never in parallel — sibling tool errors kill the close otherwise.
- **One commit per dd**: PR may bundle, but the commit trail stays 1:1 with issues.
- **Subagent briefing**: each subagent prompt must include the dd ID and instructions to run `devdash show <id>` for full context — don't re-derive scope from this plan file.
- **Dev-dash blue variant** (`f7730420`) is out of scope; user called it an experiment to pick up later. Only the dev-dash main project (`896b3dbc`) is touched.

export const notificationOps = {
  findById: (id: string) =>
    pgDb.select().from(s.notifications).where(eq(s.notifications.id, id)).then(r => r[0] ?? null),

  findByUserId: (userId: string, opts: { includeDismissed?: boolean } = {}) => {
    const where = opts.includeDismissed
      ? eq(s.notifications.userId, userId)
      : and(eq(s.notifications.userId, userId), eq(s.notifications.dismissed, false));
    return pgDb.select().from(s.notifications).where(where).orderBy(desc(s.notifications.createdAt));
  },

  findUnreadByUserId: (userId: string) =>
    pgDb.select().from(s.notifications)
      .where(and(
        eq(s.notifications.userId, userId),
        eq(s.notifications.read, false),
        eq(s.notifications.dismissed, false),
      ))
      .orderBy(desc(s.notifications.createdAt)),

  countUnread: (userId: string) =>
    pgDb.select({ count: count() }).from(s.notifications)
      .where(and(
        eq(s.notifications.userId, userId),
        eq(s.notifications.read, false),
        eq(s.notifications.dismissed, false),
      ))
      .then(r => r[0]),

  create: (id: string, userId: string, type: string, title: string, message: string | null, metadata: string | null, orgId: string | null, projectId: string | null, mentionType: string | null) =>
    pgDb.insert(s.notifications).values({ id, userId, type, title, message, metadata, orgId, projectId, mentionType }),

  markRead: (id: string) =>
    pgDb.update(s.notifications).set({ read: true }).where(eq(s.notifications.id, id)),

  markAllRead: (userId: string) =>
    pgDb.update(s.notifications).set({ read: true }).where(eq(s.notifications.userId, userId)),

  dismiss: (id: string) =>
    pgDb.update(s.notifications).set({ dismissed: true }).where(eq(s.notifications.id, id)),

  dismissAll: (userId: string) =>
    pgDb.update(s.notifications).set({ dismissed: true }).where(eq(s.notifications.userId, userId)),

  delete: (id: string) =>
    pgDb.delete(s.notifications).where(eq(s.notifications.id, id)),

  deleteOld: (userId: string, interval: string) =>
    pgDb.execute(sql`DELETE FROM notifications WHERE user_id = ${userId} AND created_at < NOW() - ${interval}::interval`),
};

# Notifications payload contract

> **Audience**: developers of dev-dash and its variant UIs (blue, red, green, yellow, pink, cli-go, …).
>
> This document defines what every notification type looks like on the wire. It is the source of truth that client-side notification rendering, click-through navigation, and SSE payload validation must build against. The type system enforces these shapes at every in-tree creation site via `MetadataFor<T>` in `packages/api-types/src/schemas/notifications.ts`.

## Shared row shape

Every notification — regardless of type — is returned to clients as:

```ts
interface Notification {
  id: string;
  userId: string;                            // target user
  type: NotificationType;                    // the discriminator (see below)
  title: string;                             // short, human-readable
  message: string | null;                    // optional longer body
  read: boolean;                             // universal user state
  dismissed: boolean;                        // universal user state
  metadata: Record<string, unknown> | null;  // shape depends on `type` — see per-type sections
  createdAt: string;                         // ISO timestamp (UTC)
}
```

`read` and `dismissed` are the only pieces of server-side user state. Everything else a client might want (mute rules, channel routing, quiet hours, digest scheduling, per-type filters) is **client-side configuration**, owned independently by each variant UI.

## Notification types

The `type` field is one of:

| Value              | Trigger                                              | Has writer? |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `agent_complete`   | Agent job finished (success, blocked, or no-op)      | ✅          |
| `agent_failed`     | Agent job failed, was rescued, or was cancelled      | ✅          |
| `task_assigned`    | Bead assigned to a user, or handed off               | ✅          |
| `mention`          | User @-mentioned in a bead comment                   | ✅          |
| `task_completed`   | (reserved — no writer today)                         | ❌          |
| `system`           | (reserved — no writer today)                         | ❌          |
| `info`             | (reserved — no writer today)                         | ❌          |

The enum lives at `packages/api-types/src/schemas/enums.ts`. Adding a new type means updating both the enum AND the `NotificationMetadataByType` map in `packages/api-types/src/schemas/notifications.ts`.

---

## Per-type metadata

### `agent_complete`

Emitted by `server/src/services/agent-dispatch.ts` when an agent job finishes. Targets dispatcher, bead assignee, and project owner (deduplicated).

```ts
type AgentCompleteMetadata = {
  jobId: string;           // always present — the agent job that finished
  projectId?: string;      // enriched by the helper
  beadId?: string;         // present iff the job was linked to a bead
  prUrl?: string;          // present on PR-merge-strategy success
  commitSha?: string;      // present on direct-push or PR success
  branchName?: string;     // present on direct-push success
  blocked?: boolean;       // true when the agent self-reported blocked
};
```

**Click-through target** (reference rule for dev-dash main UI):
- If `metadata.prUrl`, offer both "open bead" and "open PR" actions.
- Else navigate to the bead detail view at `/beads/:beadId`.
- If no `beadId` (free-form job), no navigation.

### `agent_failed`

Emitted by both `agent-dispatch.ts` (preflight / postflight / manual-cancel paths) and `job-queue.ts` (orphaned-job recovery after a server restart).

```ts
type AgentFailedMetadata = {
  jobId: string;           // always present
  projectId?: string;      // enriched by the helper
  beadId?: string;         // present iff the job was linked to a bead
  rescueBranch?: string;   // present when postflight pushed a rescue/* branch
  cancelled?: boolean;     // true when the job was manually cancelled
};
```

**Click-through target**:
- If `metadata.rescueBranch`, link to the rescue branch on GitHub (via project.githubRepo).
- Else navigate to the bead detail view.

### `task_assigned`

Emitted by `server/src/routes/beads.ts` for both direct assignment (line ~733) and handoff (line ~1108). Targets the new assignee only.

```ts
type TaskAssignedMetadata = {
  beadId: string;          // required
  projectId: string;       // required
  assignedBy?: string;     // user id of the actor; may be absent on system assigns
  handoff?: boolean;       // true when the assignment came from a handoff, not a fresh assign
};
```

**Click-through target**: `/beads/:beadId`.

### `mention`

Emitted by `server/src/routes/bead-comments.ts` when a bead comment contains `@username` that resolves to a user with project access.

```ts
type MentionMetadata = {
  beadId: string;          // required
  commentId: string;       // required — anchor to the specific comment
  projectId: string;       // required
};
```

**Click-through target**: `/beads/:beadId#comment-:commentId`.

### `task_completed`, `system`, `info`

Reserved types with no current writers. Metadata is typed as `Record<string, unknown>` (freeform). If you add a writer, also add a typed metadata schema and update this doc.

---

## How to emit a notification

**Do not call `notificationOps.create()` directly.** Use the typed helper:

```ts
import { emitNotification } from '../utils/emit-notification.js';

await emitNotification({
  userId: 'user-abc',
  type: 'task_assigned',
  title: `Assigned to you: ${bead.subject}`,
  metadata: {
    beadId: bead.id,
    projectId: project.id,
    assignedBy: actor.id,
  },
});
```

The helper:
- Generates the notification id (format: `notif-<timestamp>-<random>`).
- JSON-stringifies the metadata.
- Narrows `metadata` to `MetadataFor<T>` based on the supplied `type`, so an incorrect shape is a compile error, not a runtime surprise.
- Will gain SSE publication as a single chokepoint once real-time delivery lands (dd `03ab1f97`).

`notificationOps.create()` remains available for tests and DB seed helpers — do not deprecate it.

## Validating at boundaries

For runtime validation of a metadata blob (e.g. when accepting a notification payload from a non-trusted source — SSE receiver, external integration), use the `metadataSchemaFor(type)` helper:

```ts
import { metadataSchemaFor } from '@devdash/api-types/schemas';

const schema = metadataSchemaFor(notification.type);
const parsed = schema.safeParse(notification.metadata);
if (!parsed.success) { /* reject */ }
```

## Change process

Before adding or changing a notification type:

# Notifications payload contract

> **Audience**: developers of dev-dash and its variant UIs (blue, red, green, yellow, pink, cli-go, …).
>
> This document defines what every notification type looks like on the wire. It is the source of truth that client-side notification rendering, click-through navigation, and SSE payload validation must build against. The type system enforces these shapes at every in-tree creation site via `MetadataFor<T>` in `packages/api-types/src/schemas/notifications.ts`.

## Shared row shape

Every notification — regardless of type — is returned to clients as:

```ts
interface Notification {
  id: string;
  userId: string;                            // target user
  type: NotificationType;                    // the discriminator (see below)
  title: string;                             // short, human-readable
  message: string | null;                    // optional longer body
  read: boolean;                             // universal user state
  dismissed: boolean;                        // universal user state
  metadata: Record<string, unknown> | null;  // shape depends on `type` — see per-type sections
  createdAt: string;                         // ISO timestamp (UTC)
}
```

`read` and `dismissed` are the only pieces of server-side user state. Everything else a client might want (mute rules, channel routing, quiet hours, digest scheduling, per-type filters) is **client-side configuration**, owned independently by each variant UI.

## Notification types

The `type` field is one of:

| Value              | Trigger                                              | Has writer? |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `agent_complete`   | Agent job finished (success, blocked, or no-op)      | ✅          |
| `agent_failed`     | Agent job failed, was rescued, or was cancelled      | ✅          |
| `task_assigned`    | Bead assigned to a user, or handed off               | ✅          |
| `mention`          | User @-mentioned in a bead comment                   | ✅          |
| `task_completed`   | (reserved — no writer today)                         | ❌          |
| `system`           | (reserved — no writer today)                         | ❌          |
| `info`             | (reserved — no writer today)                         | ❌          |

The enum lives at `packages/api-types/src/schemas/enums.ts`. Adding a new type means updating both the enum AND the `NotificationMetadataByType` map in `packages/api-types/src/schemas/notifications.ts`.

---

## Per-type metadata

### `agent_complete`

Emitted by `server/src/services/agent-dispatch.ts` when an agent job finishes. Targets dispatcher, bead assignee, and project owner (deduplicated).

```ts
type AgentCompleteMetadata = {
  jobId: string;           // always present — the agent job that finished
  projectId?: string;      // enriched by the helper
  beadId?: string;         // present iff the job was linked to a bead
  prUrl?: string;          // present on PR-merge-strategy success
  commitSha?: string;      // present on direct-push or PR success
  branchName?: string;     // present on direct-push success
  blocked?: boolean;       // true when the agent self-reported blocked
};
```

**Click-through target** (reference rule for dev-dash main UI):
- If `metadata.prUrl`, offer both "open bead" and "open PR" actions.
- Else navigate to the bead detail view at `/beads/:beadId`.
- If no `beadId` (free-form job), no navigation.

### `agent_failed`

Emitted by both `agent-dispatch.ts` (preflight / postflight / manual-cancel paths) and `job-queue.ts` (orphaned-job recovery after a server restart).

```ts
type AgentFailedMetadata = {
  jobId: string;           // always present
  projectId?: string;      // enriched by the helper
  beadId?: string;         // present iff the job was linked to a bead
  rescueBranch?: string;   // present when postflight pushed a rescue/* branch
  cancelled?: boolean;     // true when the job was manually cancelled
};
```

**Click-through target**:
- If `metadata.rescueBranch`, link to the rescue branch on GitHub (via project.githubRepo).
- Else navigate to the bead detail view.

### `task_assigned`

Emitted by `server/src/routes/beads.ts` for both direct assignment (line ~733) and handoff (line ~1108). Targets the new assignee only.

```ts
type TaskAssignedMetadata = {
  beadId: string;          // required
  projectId: string;       // required
  assignedBy?: string;     // user id of the actor; may be absent on system assigns
  handoff?: boolean;       // true when the assignment came from a handoff, not a fresh assign
};
```

**Click-through target**: `/beads/:beadId`.

### `mention`

Emitted by `server/src/routes/bead-comments.ts` when a bead comment contains `@username` that resolves to a user with project access.

```ts
type MentionMetadata = {
  beadId: string;          // required
  commentId: string;       // required — anchor to the specific comment
  projectId: string;       // required
};
```

**Click-through target**: `/beads/:beadId#comment-:commentId`.

### `task_completed`, `system`, `info`

Reserved types with no current writers. Metadata is typed as `Record<string, unknown>` (freeform). If you add a writer, also add a typed metadata schema and update this doc.

---

## How to emit a notification

**Do not call `notificationOps.create()` directly.** Use the typed helper:

```ts
import { emitNotification } from '../utils/emit-notification.js';

await emitNotification({
  userId: 'user-abc',
  type: 'task_assigned',
  title: `Assigned to you: ${bead.subject}`,
  metadata: {
    beadId: bead.id,
    projectId: project.id,
    assignedBy: actor.id,
  },
});
```

The helper:
- Generates the notification id (format: `notif-<timestamp>-<random>`).
- JSON-stringifies the metadata.
- Narrows `metadata` to `MetadataFor<T>` based on the supplied `type`, so an incorrect shape is a compile error, not a runtime surprise.
- Will gain SSE publication as a single chokepoint once real-time delivery lands (dd `03ab1f97`).

`notificationOps.create()` remains available for tests and DB seed helpers — do not deprecate it.

## Validating at boundaries

For runtime validation of a metadata blob (e.g. when accepting a notification payload from a non-trusted source — SSE receiver, external integration), use the `metadataSchemaFor(type)` helper:

```ts
import { metadataSchemaFor } from '@devdash/api-types/schemas';

const schema = metadataSchemaFor(notification.type);
const parsed = schema.safeParse(notification.metadata);
if (!parsed.success) { /* reject */ }
```

## Change process

Before adding or changing a notification type:

1. Update the enum in `packages/api-types/src/schemas/enums.ts`.
2. Add or update the corresponding Zod schema and type in `packages/api-types/src/schemas/notifications.ts`.
3. Update `NotificationMetadataByType` so `MetadataFor<T>` narrows correctly.
4. Update this document.
5. Update any client-side notification rendering that does closed-set dispatching (grep for `NotificationType` in `client/src`).

# Notifications payload contract

> **Audience**: developers of dev-dash and its variant UIs (blue, red, green, yellow, pink, cli-go, …).
>
> This document defines what every notification type looks like on the wire. It is the source of truth that client-side notification rendering, click-through navigation, and SSE payload validation must build against. The type system enforces these shapes at every in-tree creation site via `MetadataFor<T>` in `packages/api-types/src/schemas/notifications.ts`.

## Shared row shape

Every notification — regardless of type — is returned to clients as:

```ts
interface Notification {
  id: string;
  userId: string;                            // target user
  type: NotificationType;                    // the discriminator (see below)
  title: string;                             // short, human-readable
  message: string | null;                    // optional longer body
  read: boolean;                             // universal user state
  dismissed: boolean;                        // universal user state
  metadata: Record<string, unknown> | null;  // shape depends on `type` — see per-type sections
  createdAt: string;                         // ISO timestamp (UTC)
}
```

`read` and `dismissed` are the only pieces of server-side user state. Everything else a client might want (mute rules, channel routing, quiet hours, digest scheduling, per-type filters) is **client-side configuration**, owned independently by each variant UI.

## Notification types

The `type` field is one of:

| Value              | Trigger                                              | Has writer? |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `agent_complete`   | Agent job finished (success, blocked, or no-op)      | ✅          |
| `agent_failed`     | Agent job failed, was rescued, or was cancelled      | ✅          |
| `task_assigned`    | Bead assigned to a user, or handed off               | ✅          |
| `mention`          | User @-mentioned in a bead comment                   | ✅          |
| `task_completed`   | (reserved — no writer today)                         | ❌          |
| `system`           | (reserved — no writer today)                         | ❌          |
| `info`             | (reserved — no writer today)                         | ❌          |

The enum lives at `packages/api-types/src/schemas/enums.ts`. Adding a new type means updating both the enum AND the `NotificationMetadataByType` map in `packages/api-types/src/schemas/notifications.ts`.

---

## Per-type metadata

### `agent_complete`

Emitted by `server/src/services/agent-dispatch.ts` when an agent job finishes. Targets dispatcher, bead assignee, and project owner (deduplicated).

```ts
type AgentCompleteMetadata = {
  jobId: string;           // always present — the agent job that finished
  projectId?: string;      // enriched by the helper
  beadId?: string;         // present iff the job was linked to a bead
  prUrl?: string;          // present on PR-merge-strategy success
  commitSha?: string;      // present on direct-push or PR success
  branchName?: string;     // present on direct-push success
  blocked?: boolean;       // true when the agent self-reported blocked
};
```

**Click-through target** (reference rule for dev-dash main UI):
- If `metadata.prUrl`, offer both "open bead" and "open PR" actions.
- Else navigate to the bead detail view at `/beads/:beadId`.
- If no `beadId` (free-form job), no navigation.

### `agent_failed`

Emitted by both `agent-dispatch.ts` (preflight / postflight / manual-cancel paths) and `job-queue.ts` (orphaned-job recovery after a server restart).

```ts
type AgentFailedMetadata = {
  jobId: string;           // always present
  projectId?: string;      // enriched by the helper
  beadId?: string;         // present iff the job was linked to a bead
  rescueBranch?: string;   // present when postflight pushed a rescue/* branch
  cancelled?: boolean;     // true when the job was manually cancelled
};
```

**Click-through target**:
- If `metadata.rescueBranch`, link to the rescue branch on GitHub (via project.githubRepo).
- Else navigate to the bead detail view.

### `task_assigned`

Emitted by `server/src/routes/beads.ts` for both direct assignment (line ~733) and handoff (line ~1108). Targets the new assignee only.

```ts
type TaskAssignedMetadata = {
  beadId: string;          // required
  projectId: string;       // required
  assignedBy?: string;     // user id of the actor; may be absent on system assigns
  handoff?: boolean;       // true when the assignment came from a handoff, not a fresh assign
};
```

**Click-through target**: `/beads/:beadId`.

### `mention`

Emitted by `server/src/routes/bead-comments.ts` when a bead comment contains `@username` that resolves to a user with project access.

```ts
type MentionMetadata = {
  beadId: string;          // required
  commentId: string;       // required — anchor to the specific comment
  projectId: string;       // required
};
```

**Click-through target**: `/beads/:beadId#comment-:commentId`.

### `task_completed`, `system`, `info`

Reserved types with no current writers. Metadata is typed as `Record<string, unknown>` (freeform). If you add a writer, also add a typed metadata schema and update this doc.

---

## How to emit a notification

**Do not call `notificationOps.create()` directly.** Use the typed helper:

```ts
import { emitNotification } from '../utils/emit-notification.js';

await emitNotification({
  userId: 'user-abc',
  type: 'task_assigned',
  title: `Assigned to you: ${bead.subject}`,
  metadata: {
    beadId: bead.id,
    projectId: project.id,
    assignedBy: actor.id,
  },
});
```

The helper:
- Generates the notification id (format: `notif-<timestamp>-<random>`).
- JSON-stringifies the metadata.
- Narrows `metadata` to `MetadataFor<T>` based on the supplied `type`, so an incorrect shape is a compile error, not a runtime surprise.
- Will gain SSE publication as a single chokepoint once real-time delivery lands (dd `03ab1f97`).

`notificationOps.create()` remains available for tests and DB seed helpers — do not deprecate it.

## Validating at boundaries

For runtime validation of a metadata blob (e.g. when accepting a notification payload from a non-trusted source — SSE receiver, external integration), use the `metadataSchemaFor(type)` helper:

```ts
import { metadataSchemaFor } from '@devdash/api-types/schemas';

const schema = metadataSchemaFor(notification.type);
const parsed = schema.safeParse(notification.metadata);
if (!parsed.success) { /* reject */ }
```

## Change process

Before adding or changing a notification type:

1. Update the enum in `packages/api-types/src/schemas/enums.ts`.
2. Add or update the corresponding Zod schema and type in `packages/api-types/src/schemas/notifications.ts`.
3. Update `NotificationMetadataByType` so `MetadataFor<T>` narrows correctly.
4. Update this document.
5. Update any client-side notification rendering that does closed-set dispatching (grep for `NotificationType` in `client/src`).

Parent epic auto-closed. Full overhaul landed — here's the summary:

## Notifications overhaul — complete

**Branch**: `worktree-notifications-overhaul` (pushed)

**Commits** (1:1 with dd issues, in dependency order):

| Commit | DD | Title |
|---|---|---|
| `c4a4b40` | `31f60032` | Migrate pre-existing beads.github_issue_id bigint drift *(incidental)* |
| `5f9d328` | `2f62374d` | Add dismissed state to notifications |
| `2384e47` | `ae2bd37e` | Add 'mention' to NotificationType shared enum |
| `75de7ea` | `051efa22` | Remove public POST /api/notifications endpoint |
| `5a8e8dc` | `d842ca69` | Wire notifications cleanup job into scheduled services |
| `ebaaaaf` | `98e41597` | Document notification payload contract and tighten metadata typing |
| `bc6071e` | `03ab1f97` | Deliver notifications over SSE; drop client polling |
| `e639944` | `1c6a6372` | Implement notification click-through in dev-dash main UI |

**What changed in reality**:
- **Contract hardened** — `mention` enum gap closed, POST creator removed (zero in-tree callers found), payload contract doc + per-type Zod schemas live at `server/docs/notifications-contract.md` and `packages/api-types/src/schemas/notifications.ts`, single typed chokepoint at `server/src/utils/emit-notification.ts`
- **Real-time** — SSE delivers full notification payloads per-user (scoping fixed so notifications don't leak between project members); polling dropped from `useNotifications` and `useUnreadCount`; client cache patched in-place via the existing `useUserSSE` EventSource
- **Lifecycle** — new `notifications-cleanup` service runs daily, prunes >90 days via `deleteOldGlobal`; `dismissed` state added schema/ops/routes/shared-types; latent `NOW() + interval` bug in `deleteOld` quietly fixed
- **Click-through** — `deriveClickTarget()` helper in `client/src/lib/notifications/` is the single rule source; bell + page both route through it; uses real anchor tags so Cmd-click works; PR/rescue-branch as secondary icon buttons with stopPropagation

**Decisions worth knowing**:
- Subagent discovered there's **no `/beads/:id` route** — bead detail is modal-only. Picked `/project/:projectId?tab=beads&bead=:beadId` as forward-compatible deep link; contract doc amended to call out that the canonical URL is aspirational.
- `agent_complete` with `prUrl` → bead is primary, PR is a secondary icon. Cmd-click each independently.
- Project GitHub repo isn't in notification metadata — needed for rescue-branch external links — so both consumers pull `useProjects()` and pass a repo map through a `ClickTargetContext`. Helper degrades to `none` when lookup fails.

**Typecheck**: clean on `server/` and `client/`. No automated test runs (per project stance that tests don't gate pushes; verification happens against live dev).

---

Want me to open the bundled PR against `main` now, or do you want to review the branch diff first? The plan's verification section calls for a deploy against dev Railway to smoke-test the SSE end-to-end and a click-through walkthrough in a browser — I can't run those from here, so those are yours regardless.

Audit complete. Everything holds up. Findings summary:

## Audit: green, with minor notes

### Correct behavior verified

- **Per-user SSE scoping** (`events.ts:63`) short-circuits `notifications:new` before the project/org/user-accessible filter — event is dropped unless `event.userId === connectionUserId`. Non-notification events unchanged. Good.
- **`project-events.ts`** extension is backward-compat — both new fields optional, existing consumers unaffected.
- **`useUserSSE.ts` cache patch** has id-dedupe on the list and a `useRef`-guarded reconnect refetch that skips the first `onopen`. Invalidate fallback on parse failure.
- **`deriveClickTarget.ts`** branches match the contract doc one-for-one. Degrades to `{kind:'none'}` on missing inputs so users never get a broken href. Uses `<Link>` for internal (react-router soft-nav) + `<a>` for external; Cmd-click opens new tab as expected.
- **Secondary action buttons** (PR / rescue branch) correctly `stopPropagation()` so they don't also fire the row's primary nav.
- **`notifications.ts` routes** — dismiss endpoints auth-gated per user; `POST /` returns 404 with a comment explaining the removal. Route order is fine despite `:id/dismiss` registered before `/dismiss-all` — Express needs two segments for `:id/dismiss` so `/dismiss-all` falls through correctly.
- **`ops.ts`** — dismiss methods added; `deleteOld` bug fix (`NOW() + interval` → `NOW() - interval`) landed; `deleteOldGlobal` is the one used by the cleanup service.
- **Migrations** — `0001_groovy_lyja.sql` is the pure bigint drift; `0002_silent_harpoon.sql` is pure dismissed column + index. Split is clean.
- **`index.ts`** — cleanup service start/stop wired in the same blocks as the other periodic services.
- **`agent-dispatch.ts` `createNotification`** is now generic on `T extends 'agent_complete' | 'agent_failed'` and each of its five internal callsites narrows correctly.
- **`notifications.contract.test.ts`** — POST tests replaced with a `seedNotification` helper and a `POST returns 404` assertion.

### Things I considered and didn't fix

- **Unread-count bump in `useUserSSE` isn't dedup-guarded** like the list is (bell.ts:61 useUserSSE.ts:85). In practice this can't double-count because the server doesn't replay events — and the reconnect-gap `invalidateQueries(['notifications', 'unread-count'])` refetches from REST anyway, correcting any drift. Not worth adding defensive code.
- **SQL files lack trailing newlines** — drizzle-kit output artifact, cosmetic.
- **`CreateNotificationBody` schema registration** in `openapi-gen.ts` — already gone (removed in `98e41597` commit).
- **No automated tests for SSE delivery or the click-through helper** — out of scope per the issues; test suite doesn't gate pushes in this project.

### Things worth calling out in the PR description

1. The `/beads/:id` aspirational URL and the query-param deep link (`/project/:projectId?tab=beads&bead=:beadId`) — contract doc amended, but reviewer should know this is the chosen forward-compat pattern.
2. The `deleteOld` bug fix that rode along with `2f62374d` (noted in the commit body).
3. The bigint-drift migration in the bundle (commit `c4a4b40`) — technically unrelated to notifications; was discovered incidentally. A reviewer seeing it and wondering "why is this here" has the answer in the commit body.
4. The SSE pipe means agents must deploy server and client together — not a breaking change per se (polling still works as a fallback because `useNotifications` does an initial REST fetch), but rolling out the server first then client later will just look like the pre-change behavior for a bit.

Ready to open the PR when you give the word. Want any changes first, or should I `gh pr create` against `main`?

gh pr create --title "Notifications system overhaul: contract, SSE, lifecycle, click-through, tests" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

End-to-end overhaul of the notifications system. Seven dd issues + two test issues + one incidental (pre-existing drift), ten commits, 1:1 commit-to-issue mapping. Parent epic: dd \`1701f49f\` (closed).

**Guiding principle** (per user direction during planning): notification **preferences** are client-side — each variant UI (blue, red, green, yellow, pink, cli-go) owns its own mute rules, filters, channels. The server's job is narrow: create, deliver, track universal state (read/dismissed). No preferences schema, no server-side routing rules, no digest/quiet-hours/channels tables.

## What changed

### Contract correctness
- Fixed the \`mention\` NotificationType enum gap (\`ae2bd37e\`). Writers had been producing rows that Zod validation silently dropped.
- Removed public \`POST /api/notifications\` — zero in-tree callers, all creation flows through \`notificationOps.create\` from services (\`051efa22\`).
- Per-type metadata Zod schemas + \`MetadataFor<T>\` type helper in \`packages/api-types\`, typed \`emitNotification()\` chokepoint at \`server/src/utils/emit-notification.ts\`, contract doc at \`server/docs/notifications-contract.md\` (\`98e41597\`).
- Every in-tree creation site (agent-dispatch, job-queue, beads × 2, bead-comments) migrated to the typed helper. \`agent-dispatch.createNotification\` is now generic on \`T extends 'agent_complete' | 'agent_failed'\` and its five internal callers are compile-checked against their event variant.

### Real-time delivery
- Notifications stream over SSE in real-time instead of polling (\`03ab1f97\`). Payload is the full wire-format \`Notification\` row; clients cache-patch in place.
- **Per-user scoping fix**: \`routes/events.ts\` now short-circuits \`notifications:new\` before project/org scoping — event is dropped unless \`event.userId === connection.user.id\`. Previously a notification meant for user A would have been delivered to every member of the same project.
- Client: \`useNotifications\` and \`useUnreadCount\` drop their 30s/15s \`refetchInterval\`. SSE listener lives in the existing \`useUserSSE\` (no second EventSource). Reconnect-gap invalidate catches events missed during transport errors.

### Lifecycle & state
- New \`dismissed\` boolean column + \`idx_notifications_user_dismissed\` index + PATCH \`/:id/dismiss\` and \`/dismiss-all\` endpoints (\`2f62374d\`). \`findByUserId\` default-excludes dismissed; pass \`?includeDismissed=true\` to override.
- New \`notificationsCleanup\` service prunes rows older than 90 days on a 24h cadence with a 5-minute initial delay (\`d842ca69\`). Retention hardcoded — no config surface.
- Incidental: fixed a latent \`NOW() + interval\` typo in \`notificationOps.deleteOld\` (would have matched only future rows). Rode along with \`2f62374d\`'s schema commit.

### Click-through reference
- New \`client/src/lib/notifications/deriveClickTarget.ts\` — single source of truth for \`Notification → URL\`, used by both the navbar bell and the full notifications page (\`1c6a6372\`).
- Anchors (not onClick divs) so Cmd/Ctrl-click opens in a new tab. Primary-action navigates to the bead; secondary icon button opens the PR (\`agent_complete\`) or rescue branch (\`agent_failed\`) with \`stopPropagation\`.
- \`agent_failed.rescueBranch\` external links resolve via a \`ClickTargetContext\` \`projectRepos\` map (pulled from \`useProjects\`) since the repo slug isn't in notification metadata. Helper degrades to \`{kind: 'none'}\` when lookup fails — users never get handed a broken href.

### Tests (new)
- **Server**: \`server/src/__tests__/notifications.sse.test.ts\` — 8 cases covering \`emitNotification\` ordering, wire shape, best-effort publish, metadata serialization, option pass-through, \`MetadataFor<T>\` narrowing. DB layer mocked via \`vi.mock\` so runs anywhere (\`03911d32\`).
- **Client**: \`client/src/lib/notifications/deriveClickTarget.test.ts\` — 30 cases covering every per-type branch of both \`deriveClickTarget\` and \`deriveSecondaryAction\`, plus edge cases for \`beadHref\` and \`githubBranchUrl\` (\`2893670d\`).

### Incidental
- \`0001_groovy_lyja.sql\` — commits the pre-existing \`beads.github_issue_id\` bigint drift from commit \`45e6b9e\`. Discovered while running \`drizzle-kit generate\` for the dismissed column; split into its own commit + dd \`31f60032\` so the notifications migration stays atomic.

## Dd issues closed

Parent epic: \`1701f49f\` — Notifications system overhaul

| DD | Commit | Title |
|---|---|---|
| \`31f60032\` | \`c4a4b40\` | Migrate pre-existing beads.github_issue_id bigint drift |
| \`2f62374d\` | \`5f9d328\` | Add dismissed state to notifications |
| \`ae2bd37e\` | \`2384e47\` | Add 'mention' to NotificationType shared enum |
| \`051efa22\` | \`75de7ea\` | Remove public POST /api/notifications endpoint |
| \`d842ca69\` | \`5a8e8dc\` | Wire notifications cleanup job into scheduled services |
| \`98e41597\` | \`ebaaaaf\` | Document notification payload contract and tighten metadata typing |
| \`03ab1f97\` | \`bc6071e\` | Deliver notifications over SSE; drop client polling |
| \`1c6a6372\` | \`e639944\` | Implement notification click-through in dev-dash main UI |
| \`03911d32\` | \`e50c51f\` | Test: notifications SSE delivery + emitNotification chokepoint |
| \`2893670d\` | \`2b5ddd0\` | Test: deriveClickTarget + deriveSecondaryAction helpers |

## Decisions worth knowing

1. **\`/beads/:beadId\` is aspirational**. This repo has no such route — bead detail is modal-only. The click-through reference implementation emits \`/project/:projectId?tab=beads&bead=:beadId\` as a forward-compatible deep link. Contract doc was amended with a \"URL patterns\" section calling this out. Future work can honor \`?bead=\` to auto-open the modal, or add a real route, without changing the contract.
2. **\`agent_complete\` with a PR** uses the bead as the primary target and surfaces the PR as a secondary icon button (\`GitPullRequest\`). Cmd-click each independently. Same pattern for \`agent_failed\` + rescue branch (\`GitBranch\`).
3. **Server deploy must precede client deploy** — the client hook still does an initial REST fetch so an old client against the new server keeps working, but a new client against an old server would just look like the pre-change polling behavior until the server catches up. Not a breaking change, just sequencing.
4. **Variant UIs are on their own for preference/config UIs.** This PR lands the server contract they can build against; each variant decides how to surface muting, filtering, channel routing, etc. in its own codebase.

## Test plan

---
name: CI test DB — persistent Railway replica, not ephemeral containers
description: Test DB for CI should be a long-lived Railway replica kept separate from prod; don't propose per-run Postgres service containers
type: feedback
---

When CI needs a test database, **use a persistent Railway replica DB** that is isolated from prod — NOT a fresh Postgres service container spun up per CI run.

**Why:** Ephemeral service containers have ~10s per-run spin-up cost plus a full schema re-apply (36 tables for dev-dash). That adds up over many CI runs. A persistent replica avoids all of that: the DB is always available, tests just need to clean up after themselves (tests already TRUNCATE their per-file data via setupTestApp/cleanup), and CI only needs to apply any pending migrations at the start of each run.

**Constraints (critical):**
- The replica must be a **separate database from prod**, never the prod URL — the user has explicitly said not to alter prod from CI under any circumstance.
- Migrations applied to the replica should be idempotent (use `IF NOT EXISTS` / `IF EXISTS` / safely repeatable patterns) so they can be re-run each CI invocation without blowing up.
- The dev-dash `integration-tests` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` uses `secrets.POSTGRES_URL` which is (per commit `9990050`) the dedicated test DB, not prod.

**How to apply:** When a PR adds drizzle migrations, also add a CI step that applies those migrations against `secrets.POSTGRES_URL` before tests run. Rewrite the migration SQL to be idempotent (e.g. `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`) so re-running across many CI invocations is a no-op. Do NOT propose replacing the Railway replica with a per-run `services.postgres` service container — that was explicitly rejected on 2026-04-11 during the notifications overhaul PR review.
