# Notifications payload contract

> **Audience**: developers of dev-dash and its variant UIs (blue, red, green, yellow, pink, cli-go, …).
>
> This document defines what every notification type looks like on the wire. It is the source of truth that client-side notification rendering, click-through navigation, and SSE payload validation must build against. The type system enforces these shapes at every in-tree creation site via `MetadataFor<T>` in `packages/api-types/src/schemas/notifications.ts`.

## Shared row shape

Every notification — regardless of type — is returned to clients as:

```ts
interface Notification {
  id: string;
  userId: string;                            // target user
  type: NotificationType;                    // the discriminator (see below)
  title: string;                             // short, human-readable
  message: string | null;                    // optional longer body
  read: boolean;                             // universal user state
  dismissed: boolean;                        // universal user state
  metadata: Record<string, unknown> | null;  // shape depends on `type` — see per-type sections
  createdAt: string;                         // ISO timestamp (UTC)
}
```

`read` and `dismissed` are the only pieces of server-side user state. Everything else a client might want (mute rules, channel routing, quiet hours, digest scheduling, per-type filters) is **client-side configuration**, owned independently by each variant UI.

## Notification types

The `type` field is one of:

| Value              | Trigger                                              | Has writer? |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `agent_complete`   | Agent job finished (success, blocked, or no-op)      | ✅          |
| `agent_failed`     | Agent job failed, was rescued, or was cancelled      | ✅          |
| `task_assigned`    | Bead assigned to a user, or handed off               | ✅          |
| `mention`          | User @-mentioned in a bead comment                   | ✅          |
| `task_completed`   | (reserved — no writer today)                         | ❌          |
| `system`           | (reserved — no writer today)                         | ❌          |
| `info`             | (reserved — no writer today)                         | ❌          |

The enum lives at `packages/api-types/src/schemas/enums.ts`. Adding a new type means updating both the enum AND the `NotificationMetadataByType` map in `packages/api-types/src/schemas/notifications.ts`.

---

## URL patterns

The click-through rules below reference `/beads/:beadId` as the canonical target for bead detail views. **This is aspirational** — dev-dash main UI today renders bead detail as a modal triggered from the project's Beads tab, not as a routable page. The reference implementation in `client/src/lib/notifications/deriveClickTarget.ts` therefore emits a forward-compatible deep link of the form `/project/:projectId?tab=beads&bead=:beadId`, which lands the user on the correct project's Beads tab. A follow-up is expected to honor the `?bead=` query param and auto-open the modal; at that point the deep link can be simplified, and if a dedicated `/beads/:beadId` route is ever added, clients can migrate to it without touching this contract.

Mention anchors are appended as `#comment-:commentId` regardless of the outer URL pattern.

## Per-type metadata

### `agent_complete`

Emitted by `server/src/services/agent-dispatch.ts` when an agent job finishes. Targets dispatcher, bead assignee, and project owner (deduplicated).

```ts
type AgentCompleteMetadata = {
  jobId: string;           // always present — the agent job that finished
  projectId: string;       // REQUIRED — the click-through helper needs it
  beadId?: string;         // present iff the job was linked to a bead
  prUrl?: string;          // present on PR-merge-strategy success
  commitSha?: string;      // present on direct-push or PR success
  branchName?: string;     // present on direct-push success
  blocked?: boolean;       // true when the agent self-reported blocked
};
```

> **Why `projectId` is required**: see dd `0cf7f8e0`. ~141 old notifications shipped without `projectId`, causing every click to fall through to `/dashboard` instead of opening the bead. After the data backfill, the schema was tightened so a future writer omitting it is a TypeScript compile error rather than a silent runtime degradation.

**Click-through target** (reference rule for dev-dash main UI):
- If `metadata.prUrl`, offer both "open bead" and "open PR" actions.
- Else navigate to the bead detail view at `/beads/:beadId`.
- If no `beadId` (free-form job), no navigation.

### `agent_failed`

Emitted by both `agent-dispatch.ts` (preflight / postflight / manual-cancel paths) and `job-queue.ts` (orphaned-job recovery after a server restart).

```ts
type AgentFailedMetadata = {
  jobId: string;           // always present
  projectId: string;       // REQUIRED — same reason as AgentCompleteMetadata above
  beadId?: string;         // present iff the job was linked to a bead
  rescueBranch?: string;   // present when postflight pushed a rescue/* branch
  cancelled?: boolean;     // true when the job was manually cancelled
};
```

**Click-through target**:
- If `metadata.rescueBranch`, link to the rescue branch on GitHub (via project.githubRepo).
- Else navigate to the bead detail view.

### `task_assigned`

Emitted by `server/src/routes/beads.ts` for both direct assignment (line ~733) and handoff (line ~1108). Targets the new assignee only.

```ts
type TaskAssignedMetadata = {
  beadId: string;          // required
  projectId: string;       // required
  assignedBy?: string;     // user id of the actor; may be absent on system assigns
  handoff?: boolean;       // true when the assignment came from a handoff, not a fresh assign
};
```

**Click-through target**: `/beads/:beadId`.

### `mention`

Emitted by `server/src/routes/bead-comments.ts` when a bead comment contains `@username` that resolves to a user with project access.

```ts
type MentionMetadata = {
  beadId: string;          // required
  commentId: string;       // required — anchor to the specific comment
  projectId: string;       // required
};
```

**Click-through target**: `/beads/:beadId#comment-:commentId`.

### `task_completed`, `system`, `info`

Reserved types with no current writers. Metadata is typed as `Record<string, unknown>` (freeform). If you add a writer, also add a typed metadata schema and update this doc.

---

## How to emit a notification

**Do not call `notificationOps.create()` directly.** Use the typed helper:

```ts
import { emitNotification } from '../utils/emit-notification.js';

await emitNotification({
  userId: 'user-abc',
  type: 'task_assigned',
  title: `Assigned to you: ${bead.subject}`,
  metadata: {
    beadId: bead.id,
    projectId: project.id,
    assignedBy: actor.id,
  },
});
```

The helper:

# Notifications payload contract

> **Audience**: developers of dev-dash and its variant UIs (blue, red, green, yellow, pink, cli-go, …).
>
> This document defines what every notification type looks like on the wire. It is the source of truth that client-side notification rendering, click-through navigation, and SSE payload validation must build against. The type system enforces these shapes at every in-tree creation site via `MetadataFor<T>` in `packages/api-types/src/schemas/notifications.ts`.

## Shared row shape

Every notification — regardless of type — is returned to clients as:

```ts
interface Notification {
  id: string;
  userId: string;                            // target user
  type: NotificationType;                    // the discriminator (see below)
  title: string;                             // short, human-readable
  message: string | null;                    // optional longer body
  read: boolean;                             // universal user state
  dismissed: boolean;                        // universal user state
  metadata: Record<string, unknown> | null;  // shape depends on `type` — see per-type sections
  createdAt: string;                         // ISO timestamp (UTC)
}
```

`read` and `dismissed` are the only pieces of server-side user state. Everything else a client might want (mute rules, channel routing, quiet hours, digest scheduling, per-type filters) is **client-side configuration**, owned independently by each variant UI.

## Notification types

The `type` field is one of:

| Value                  | Tier | Trigger                                              | Has writer? |
| ---------------------- | ---- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `agent_complete`       | 2    | Agent job finished (success, blocked, or no-op)      | ✅          |
| `agent_failed`         | 2    | Agent job failed, was rescued, or was cancelled      | ✅          |
| `task_status_changed`  | 1    | Bead transitioned between statuses                   | ❌ (pending)|
| `comment_added`        | 1    | Someone commented on a bead you own/are assigned to  | ❌ (pending)|
| `dependency_resolved`  | 1    | A blocking bead completed, unblocking your bead      | ❌ (pending)|
| `task_assigned`        | 3    | Bead assigned to a user, or handed off               | ✅          |
| `priority_changed`     | 3    | Bead priority changed by someone other than assignee | ❌ (pending)|
| `mention`              | 3    | User @-mentioned in a bead comment                   | ✅          |
| `member_joined`        | 3    | Someone joined the project                           | ❌ (pending)|
| `member_left`          | 3    | Someone left or was removed from the project         | ❌ (pending)|
| `system`               |      | (reserved — no writer today)                         | ❌          |
| `info`                 |      | (reserved — no writer today)                         | ❌          |

Tier 1 = collaboration essentials (team plan). Tier 2 = agent events (agent plan). Tier 3 = lifecycle + nice-to-have. Pending types have schemas defined but no server-side writer yet; see child issues under dd `24b13281`.

The enum lives at `packages/api-types/src/schemas/enums.ts`. Adding a new type means updating both the enum AND the `NotificationMetadataByType` map in `packages/api-types/src/schemas/notifications.ts`.

---

## URL patterns

The click-through rules below reference `/beads/:beadId` as the canonical target for bead detail views. **This is aspirational** — dev-dash main UI today renders bead detail as a modal triggered from the project's Beads tab, not as a routable page. The reference implementation in `client/src/lib/notifications/deriveClickTarget.ts` therefore emits a forward-compatible deep link of the form `/project/:projectId?tab=beads&bead=:beadId`, which lands the user on the correct project's Beads tab. A follow-up is expected to honor the `?bead=` query param and auto-open the modal; at that point the deep link can be simplified, and if a dedicated `/beads/:beadId` route is ever added, clients can migrate to it without touching this contract.

Mention anchors are appended as `#comment-:commentId` regardless of the outer URL pattern.

## Per-type metadata

### `agent_complete`

Emitted by `server/src/services/agent-dispatch.ts` when an agent job finishes. Targets dispatcher, bead assignee, and project owner (deduplicated).

```ts
type AgentCompleteMetadata = {
  jobId: string;           // always present — the agent job that finished
  projectId: string;       // REQUIRED — the click-through helper needs it
  beadId?: string;         // present iff the job was linked to a bead
  prUrl?: string;          // present on PR-merge-strategy success
  commitSha?: string;      // present on direct-push or PR success
  branchName?: string;     // present on direct-push success
  blocked?: boolean;       // true when the agent self-reported blocked
};
```

> **Why `projectId` is required**: see dd `0cf7f8e0`. ~141 old notifications shipped without `projectId`, causing every click to fall through to `/dashboard` instead of opening the bead. After the data backfill, the schema was tightened so a future writer omitting it is a TypeScript compile error rather than a silent runtime degradation.

**Click-through target** (reference rule for dev-dash main UI):
- If `metadata.prUrl`, offer both "open bead" and "open PR" actions.
- Else navigate to the bead detail view at `/beads/:beadId`.
- If no `beadId` (free-form job), no navigation.

### `agent_failed`

Emitted by both `agent-dispatch.ts` (preflight / postflight / manual-cancel paths) and `job-queue.ts` (orphaned-job recovery after a server restart).

```ts
type AgentFailedMetadata = {
  jobId: string;           // always present
  projectId: string;       // REQUIRED — same reason as AgentCompleteMetadata above
  beadId?: string;         // present iff the job was linked to a bead
  rescueBranch?: string;   // present when postflight pushed a rescue/* branch
  cancelled?: boolean;     // true when the job was manually cancelled
};
```

**Click-through target**:
- If `metadata.rescueBranch`, link to the rescue branch on GitHub (via project.githubRepo).
- Else navigate to the bead detail view.

### `task_assigned`

Emitted by `server/src/routes/beads.ts` for both direct assignment (line ~733) and handoff (line ~1108). Targets the new assignee only.

```ts
type TaskAssignedMetadata = {
  beadId: string;          // required
  projectId: string;       // required
  assignedBy?: string;     // user id of the actor; may be absent on system assigns
  handoff?: boolean;       // true when the assignment came from a handoff, not a fresh assign
};
```

**Click-through target**: `/beads/:beadId`.

### `mention`

Emitted by `server/src/routes/bead-comments.ts` when a bead comment contains `@username` that resolves to a user with project access.

```ts
type MentionMetadata = {
  beadId: string;          // required
  commentId: string;       // required — anchor to the specific comment
  projectId: string;       // required
};
```

**Click-through target**: `/beads/:beadId#comment-:commentId`.

### `task_completed`, `system`, `info`

Reserved types with no current writers. Metadata is typed as `Record<string, unknown>` (freeform). If you add a writer, also add a typed metadata schema and update this doc.

---

## How to emit a notification

**Do not call `notificationOps.create()` directly.** Use the typed helper:

```ts
import { emitNotification } from '../utils/emit-notification.js';

await emitNotification({
  userId: 'user-abc',
  type: 'task_assigned',
  title: `Assigned to you: ${bead.subject}`,
  metadata: {
    beadId: bead.id,
    projectId: project.id,
    assignedBy: actor.id,
  },
});
```

The helper:
- Generates the notification id (format: `notif-<timestamp>-<random>`).
- JSON-stringifies the metadata.
- Narrows `metadata` to `MetadataFor<T>` based on the supplied `type`, so an incorrect shape is a compile error, not a runtime surprise.
- Will gain SSE publication as a single chokepoint once real-time delivery lands (dd `03ab1f97`).

`notificationOps.create()` remains available for tests and DB seed helpers — do not deprecate it.

## Validating at boundaries

For runtime validation of a metadata blob (e.g. when accepting a notification payload from a non-trusted source — SSE receiver, external integration), use the `metadataSchemaFor(type)` helper:

```ts
import { metadataSchemaFor } from '@devdash/api-types/schemas';

const schema = metadataSchemaFor(notification.type);
const parsed = schema.safeParse(notification.metadata);
if (!parsed.success) { /* reject */ }
```

## Change process

Before adding or changing a notification type:

1. Update the enum in `packages/api-types/src/schemas/enums.ts`.
2. Add or update the corresponding Zod schema and type in `packages/api-types/src/schemas/notifications.ts`.
3. Update `NotificationMetadataByType` so `MetadataFor<T>` narrows correctly.
4. Update this document.
5. Update any client-side notification rendering that does closed-set dispatching (grep for `NotificationType` in `client/src`).

## Summary

Phase 1 of the notification taxonomy expansion (parent epic dd \`24b13281\`). Removes the unused \`task_completed\` type, adds 6 new types for the full collaboration lifecycle, wires client rendering for all of them, and adds the \`projectMemberOps.hasMultipleMembers()\` gate that Phase 2+3 writers will use.

No server-side writers yet — this PR lays the foundation so the writers have a settled schema, client, and contract to emit against.

## New notification types

| Type | Tier | What it covers | Writer status |
|---|---|---|---|
| \`task_status_changed\` | 1 | Bead transitioned between statuses | Pending (dd \`06a366c1\`) |
| \`comment_added\` | 1 | Comment on a bead you own/are assigned to | Pending (dd \`9de3a87c\`) |
| \`dependency_resolved\` | 1 | Blocking bead completed, unblocking yours | Pending (dd \`4e4f89a4\`) |
| \`priority_changed\` | 3 | Bead priority changed by someone else | Pending (dd \`4b60b3a0\`) |
| \`member_joined\` | 3 | Someone joined your project | Pending (dd \`e5395fff\`) |
| \`member_left\` | 3 | Someone left or was removed | Pending (dd \`e5395fff\`) |

## What changed (2 commits)

### Commit 1 — Schema + client rendering (refs: dd \`47621e54\`, \`bcc66a57\`)

**Shared types** (\`packages/api-types\`):
- \`NotificationType\` enum: remove \`task_completed\`, add 6 new values, organized by tier
- 6 new Zod metadata schemas with fully typed fields
- \`NotificationMetadataByType\` map + \`metadataSchemaFor()\` switch updated

**Contract doc** (\`server/docs/notifications-contract.md\`):
- Type table with tier column, all new types with "pending" writers
- Per-type sections with metadata shapes, click-through rules, trigger sites, gating notes

**Client** (5 files):
- \`MobileActivityScreen.tsx\`: exhaustive \`Record<NotificationType, ...>\` maps
- \`NotificationBell.tsx\`: \`getNotificationIcon\` switch
- \`Notifications.tsx\`: filter chips (reordered collaboration-first), icon switch, \`NotificationMetadataDetails\` per-type pills (status transition badge, priority escalation, role badge, etc.)
- \`deriveClickTarget.ts\`: bead-related types → internal bead link; \`comment_added\` includes \`#comment-<id>\` anchor; member events → \`/project/:id?tab=settings\`
- \`deriveClickTarget.test.ts\`: 11 new test cases — **41 total** (was 30)

### Commit 2 — Multi-member gate helper (refs: dd \`40da63b6\`)

**\`server/src/db/ops.ts\`**: new \`projectMemberOps.hasMultipleMembers(projectId)\` — returns \`true\` when \`COUNT(*) > 1\` on \`project_members\`. Phase 2+3 writers will call this alongside the "don't notify the actor" rule so solo free-tier users don't accumulate notification rows nobody will ever read.

## Design decisions

1. **\`task_completed\` retired, not aliased**: zero writers, zero DB rows, 19 dead references. The more general \`task_status_changed\` (with \`fromStatus\`/\`toStatus\` in metadata) covers all transitions including completion.

2. **Filter dropdown reordered**: collaboration types first (Status Changed, Comments, Unblocked, Assigned, Priority, Mentions), then agent events, then member events, then reserved. Reflects the priority for team users.

3. **No caching on hasMultipleMembers**: single SQL query per call. If batch status updates cause N+1, a TTL cache can be added later without changing the call-site API.

Here are the three code locations you need for implementing notification writers:

### 1. Bead Status Transitions (beads.ts)

**File:** `/Users/jason/playground/claudespace/dev-dash/server/src/routes/beads.ts`

**Status extraction and comparison:**
- **Line 589:** Status extracted from request body: `const { projectId, status, ... } = req.body`
- **Line 597:** Existing bead fetched: `const existing = await beadOps.findById(req.params.id as string)`
- **Line 665:** Status comparison happens here: `if (status === 'completed' && existing.status !== 'completed')`
- **Line 749:** Non-completion status changes detected: `if (status && status !== existing.status && status !== 'completed')`

**Update mechanism:**
- Uses `transitionStatus()` helper (imported from `bead-lifecycle.ts`) for completion/archived transitions
- Direct `beadOps.updateFull()` for other fields including status (line 681-696)

**Existing pattern:**
- **Lines 748-759:** Already logs `bead.status_changed` activity on status transitions (except completion)
- **Lines 665-673:** Completion delegates to `transitionStatus()` which handles cascading

**Existing `task_assigned` notification:**
- **Lines 770-784:** Emits `task_assigned` notification when `assignedTo` changes (separate from status)
- Pattern: `await emitNotification({ userId, type: 'task_assigned', title, metadata, ... })`

**Pre-update bead variable:**
- `existing` holds the bead before update (fetched at line 597)
- `status` is the new status from request body
- **Optimal location for `task_status_changed` emitter:** After line 759, after status change logging but before line 762 (before assignedTo handling)

### 2. blockedBy Storage Format

**Schema:** `/Users/jason/playground/claudespace/dev-dash/server/src/db/schema.ts`, line 260
```
blockedBy: text('blocked_by')
```

**Format:** JSON array stored as text string (parsed with `JSON.parse()`)
- Example in beads.ts line 154: `blockedBy: row.blockedBy ? JSON.parse(row.blockedBy) : []`
- Stored as `JSON.stringify(blockedBy)` when updating

**Finding dependent beads:**
- **No separate table** — `blockedBy` and `blocks` are the only dependency storage
- **Query pattern in bead-lifecycle.ts lines 142-165:** When a bead completes, finds dependents via its `blocks` array, then removes completed bead from their `blockedBy` arrays
- **Batch fetch pattern (line 145):** 
  ```typescript
  const blocksIds: string[] = bead.blocks ? JSON.parse(bead.blocks) : [];
  const deps = await pgDb.execute(sql`SELECT * FROM beads WHERE id IN (${sql.join(blocksIds.map(id => sql`${id}`), sql`, `)})`) as any;
  ```

**Dependency resolution on completion:**
- **Lines 142-164 (bead-lifecycle.ts):** When bead completes, iterates `blocks` array, updates each dependent's `blockedBy` array by removing the completed ID
- **Line 158-162:** If `blockedBy` becomes empty and status is 'blocked', transitions to 'pending'

**Grep results show no separate dependency table** — all logic is in bead-lifecycle.ts lines 142-164 (cascade on completion) and lines 273-298 (cleanup on deletion).

### 3. Bead-Comments POST Handler

**File:** `/Users/jason/playground/claudespace/dev-dash/server/src/routes/bead-comments.ts`

**Create-comment handler:**
- **Lines 85-159:** Full POST handler
- **Lines 101-110:** Comment creation
- **Lines 126-151:** Mention notification logic (your stated range of 125-149 is correct)

**Bead variable:**
- **Line 96:** `const bead = await beadOps.findById(beadId)` — holds commented-on bead
- Available in scope for reading assignee/owner at lines 100-159

**Bead creator/owner lookup:**
- **No separate lookup needed** — `bead.owner` and `bead.assignedTo` are available from the fetched bead (line 96)
- If you need user details (displayName), pattern is lines 113-114: fetch user via `userOps.findById()`, as done for comment author

## Summary

Phase 2 of the notification taxonomy expansion (parent epic dd \`24b13281\`). Wires the three Tier 1 collaboration notification writers — the events that make the notification center useful for team users who don't use the agent pipeline.

Three commits, one per dd issue, each touching a different trigger file.

## Commit 1 — \`task_status_changed\` (dd \`06a366c1\`)

**File:** \`server/src/routes/beads.ts\`

Fires after both the completion (\`transitionStatus\`) and non-completion (\`updateFull\`) code paths. A single block after the if/else catches every status transition.

- **Targets:** bead assignee + project owner (deduped)
- **Excludes:** the actor who changed the status
- **Gate:** \`projectMemberOps.hasMultipleMembers()\` — solo projects generate zero rows
- **Title:** \`"Fix login bug: in_progress → completed"\`
- **Metadata:** \`{ beadId, projectId, fromStatus, toStatus, changedBy }\`

## Commit 2 — \`comment_added\` (dd \`9de3a87c\`)

**File:** \`server/src/routes/bead-comments.ts\`

Broader than @mentions — notifies bead assignee + project owner of ANY comment, not just ones that @-mention them.

- **Dedup against mentions:** \`mentionedUserIds\` hoisted above the mention try-block so the comment_added block can exclude anyone who already got a mention notification for the same comment
- **Targets:** bead assignee + project owner (deduped)
- **Excludes:** the commenter + already-mentioned users
- **Gate:** \`projectMemberOps.hasMultipleMembers()\`
- **Title:** \`"New comment on <subject>"\`
- **Metadata:** \`{ beadId, commentId, projectId, commentedBy }\`

## Commit 3 — \`dependency_resolved\` (dd \`4e4f89a4\`)

**File:** \`server/src/services/bead-lifecycle.ts\`

Fires inside the existing cascade block where a dependent bead's \`blockedBy\` array becomes empty and transitions from blocked → pending.

- **Targets:** the dependent bead's assignee
- **Excludes:** the actor who completed the blocking bead
- **Gate:** \`projectMemberOps.hasMultipleMembers()\` on the **dependent bead's** project (handles cross-project deps)
- **Title:** \`"Unblocked: <dependent subject>"\`
- **Message:** \`"Dependency \"<completed subject>\" completed"\`

- **Note:** dependent rows come from raw \`pgDb.execute()\` so columns are snake_case (\`dep.assigned_to\`, \`dep.project_id\`)

## Common patterns across all three

- All wrapped in try/catch — notification failure never blocks the underlying operation
- All call \`emitNotification()\` through the typed chokepoint so metadata shape is compile-checked
- All use the "don't notify the actor" rule consistently
- All gated by \`projectMemberOps.hasMultipleMembers()\` so solo users stay quiet

- [ ] On a single-member project: none of the above produces notifications
- [ ] An actor changing their own bead's status does not self-notify

Refs: dd \`06a366c1\`, \`9de3a87c\`, \`4e4f89a4\`

## Summary

Phase 3 of the notification taxonomy expansion (parent epic dd \`24b13281\`). Wires the two remaining Tier 3 notification writers. After this PR, every type in the expanded taxonomy has a server-side writer — only the Phase 4 audit pass remains.

Two commits, one per dd issue.

## Commit 1 — \`priority_changed\` (dd \`4b60b3a0\`)

**File:** \`server/src/routes/beads.ts\`

Fires in the PATCH handler when \`priority !== existing.priority\`. Targets the bead assignee only (not project owner — priority is most relevant to the person doing the work). Excludes the actor. Gated by \`hasMultipleMembers()\`.

- **Title:** \`"Priority changed: <subject>"\`
- **Message:** \`"Medium → Critical"\` (human-readable labels)
- **Metadata:** \`{ beadId, projectId, fromPriority, toPriority, changedBy }\`

## Commit 2 — \`member_joined\` + \`member_left\` (dd \`e5395fff\`)

**Files:** \`server/src/routes/projects.ts\`, \`server/src/routes/auth.ts\`

\`member_joined\` — two trigger sites:
1. **projects.ts direct-add** (existing-user path): notify project owner after \`projectMemberOps.add()\`
2. **auth.ts invitation-redeem** (OAuth login): for each redeemed invitation, look up the project and notify the owner

\`member_left\` — one trigger site:
- **projects.ts remove-member**: notifies the **removed user**, not the project owner. The owner is always the actor here (\`requireProjectOwner\` gates the endpoint), so notifying them would be a self-notification. The removed user benefits from knowing they lost access. **This is a deliberate deviation from the dd description** which said "notify project owner" — followed the spirit of the "don't notify the actor" rule instead.

No multi-member gate on member events: \`member_joined\` IS the event that makes a project multi-member, and \`member_left\` should still reach the removed user even on a 2→1 transition.

## Test plan

- [x] \`npx tsc --noEmit -p server/tsconfig.json\` — clean

- [ ] Solo project priority change → no notification
- [ ] Add a member to a project (direct add) → owner gets \`member_joined\`
- [ ] New user redeems invitation via OAuth → each project owner gets \`member_joined\`
- [ ] Remove a member → the removed user gets \`member_left\`

Refs: dd \`4b60b3a0\`, \`e5395fff\`

Notification taxonomy expansion complete. All four phases shipped.

## Final state of parent epic `24b13281`

| Phase | DD | Title | Status | PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `47621e54` | Schema + 6 new types | Closed | #634 |
| 1 | `40da63b6` | hasMultipleMembers() helper | Closed | #634 |
| 1 | `bcc66a57` | Client rendering | Closed | #634 |

| 2 | `9de3a87c` | comment_added writer | Closed | #635 |
| 2 | `4e4f89a4` | dependency_resolved writer | Closed | #635 |
| 3 | `4b60b3a0` | priority_changed writer | Closed | #636 |
| 3 | `e5395fff` | member_joined + member_left writers | Closed | #636 |
| 4 | `0cf9c7e9` | Audit: activity_log coverage | Closed | #637 |

**9 issues, 4 PRs, all merged and deployed.** The notification system now covers the full collaboration lifecycle — not just agent events.

### What a user experiences now

| User type | What they see in the bell |
|---|---|
| **Solo free** | Nothing — multi-member gate keeps the bell quiet |
| **Solo + agents** | Agent completions, failures, rescues |
| **Team (no agents)** | Status changes, comments, priority changes, dependency unblocks, member joins/leaves, @mentions, task assignments |
| **Team + agents** | Everything above |
